slides.title: Three authors, one trail
slides.text: Your footprint is written by three authors: you, in your own posts; other people, in posts about you; and services, collecting scores, locations and likes.

slides.title: Who wrote this clue?
slides.text: Pim found three clues in one trail. Each clue has a different author.
steps: you share your race photo: you
a friend tags you in theirs: a friend
a game saves your top score: a service

slides.title: Delete is not erase
slides.text: Deleting a post is asking nicely for it to go. Copies, screenshots and shares can keep it alive long after your own copy is gone.
slides.alt: Would you rather: delete an old post you are embarrassed by, or leave it and laugh?

focus.cue: Deleting asks nicely for a post to go
Copies and screenshots can keep it alive

slides.title: Future readers
slides.text: That drawing you posted for feedback stays in your trail. Years later, teammates, schools and employers may read old posts as part of who you are.

visual.label: Years later, who reads the drawing you posted?

focus.cue: Today: you post a drawing for feedback

slides.title: Ask before you post
slides.text: Public gets you seen and found; private keeps you safe. Before you post, ask the Cyber Defender question: what could someone do with this?
slides.alt: A post from Fan Club, “Hello, skateboard star!”, with clues marked: things it knows about you, and your mailbox key.

focus.cue: A post built from someone's public profile
What could someone do with this?

words.means: everything about you that can be found online
lasting a very long time, even after deleting
what people think of you, based on what they find
everyone who can see what you shared, now or later

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Escape the Post Office at Lock 3: Which Pim? One card wears a faked postmark. Check every clue in each trail, then pick the real Pim.
slides.alt: Three messages say they are from Pim; one wears a faked trail. A card from Pim asks you to bring your mailbox key to a side gate.

focus.cue: Play Which Pim?: trust the trail, not the name
